clue.text: Limited fish round north (not coarse)

indicators.note: the fish is placed round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: cod is a common sea fish
something not coarse is fine, as in fine sand

explanation.surface: An angler restricted to sea fish, being told coarse fishing is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the fish around the other two pieces. 'Coarse' looks like angling slang for freshwater fishing, but here it just wants its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confined is restricted or kept within bounds.

clue.text: Cheese almost all cut

indicators.note: almost all of the word means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: cut short, as in a brief meeting

explanation.surface: Nearly all the cheese has been sliced up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' drops the last letter F from BRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Avoid last couple of cigarettes and some tobacco

indicators.note: the last couple of letters of the word are taken, here its final two

parts.note: a chew is a plug of tobacco for chewing

explanation.surface: A smoker trying to quit, down to the last few cigarettes and a little tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last couple of' takes ES, the final two letters of 'cigarettes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to shun or abstain from it.

clue.text: Narrow obsession's no good

indicators.note: no good says the letter for good is to be taken away

parts.note: having a thing about something is an obsession; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone's fixation turns out to be harmful and restrictive.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and narrow are synonyms, as in a thin strip.

clue.text: Hard to get rid of, smoothly move in as this?

definitions.text: Hard to get rid of, smoothly move in as this?

parts.words: Hard to get rid of, smoothly move in as this?
parts.note: a visitor who settles in easily under your roof and then never leaves; the person is the one who comes to stay

explanation.surface: A guide to settling into a new home without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as advice on moving house, but it describes the guest who will not go.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor staying overnight or longer in someone's home, here one who overstays.

clue.text: Plump tenor engaged in part song

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so the tenor goes inside

parts.note: a round is a song in which voices enter in turn, singing in parts

explanation.surface: A portly tenor singing in a choral piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means round and fat, the same as plump.

clue.text: Wild flowers climbed among shadows

indicators.note: among puts the climbing word inside the shadows word

parts.note: to dog someone is to shadow or follow them
rose is the past tense of rise, to climb

explanation.surface: Wild plants have grown up through the shady places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' sets the climbing word inside the other; 'shadows' is a verb meaning follows, not dark patches.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog rose is a wild climbing rose of European hedgerows.

clue.text: To show violence towards jazz great's out of order

indicators.note: the name's parts are out of their usual order, the front section moved to the back

parts.note: Louis Armstrong was a great jazz trumpeter; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A jazz legend has behaved badly enough to be violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' moves ARM from the front of ARMSTRONG to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To strong-arm someone is to use force or intimidation on them.

clue.text: Jinx found in gangster circles

parts.note: hood is slang for a hoodlum or gangster
O looks like a circle, so two circles give two of them

explanation.surface: Bad luck turns up among the mob's inner groups.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a thing or person that brings bad luck.

clue.text: Take off Rector and laugh impudently

parts.note: to take off is to run away

explanation.surface: Mock a clergyman by taking him off, then sneer at him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests mimicry, but it means run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleer is an old word for to grin or jeer mockingly.

clue.text: Dispenses with workers on strike

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands
striking workers are out

explanation.surface: A boss does without staff who have walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispenses with' looks like 'does without', but only 'Dispenses' is the definition; 'with' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands out means distributes or gives out, as a dispenser does.

clue.text: Not recognised from glance down, duke in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duke in disguise slips by unrecognised, eyes lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disguise' rearranges GLANCE, DOWN and DUKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unacknowledged means not admitted or not given recognition.

clue.text: King I captured in awfully accurate and unflattering portrait

indicators.note: captured in means held inside, so king and I go within the other letters
awfully means badly done, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch caught in a painfully true portrait he did not like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges ACCURATE; 'captured in' puts R and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature exaggerates features to mock, the opposite of a flattering likeness.

clue.text: Practical means to an end

definitions.meaning: convenient and useful rather than principled
a device or measure taken to reach a goal

explanation.definitionFit: An expedient is a handy measure, and as an adjective it means advantageous or practical.

clue.text: Germany's citified port in Africa

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
urban means belonging to a city

explanation.surface: A German-owned, city-style harbour on the African coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Durban is a major South African port.
explanation.definitionFit: Durban is a large seaport in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

clue.text: Feast that may cover bed

definitions.meaning: a lavish meal laid out for guests
a bedspread or cover laid over a bed

explanation.definitionFit: A spread is both a big meal laid on the table and a bedcover.

clue.text: Nodding off as terrible din grows

indicators.note: terrible means badly made, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone dozing while the racket gets louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsing means dozing or falling lightly asleep.

clue.text: Advice about routine, including finish at one

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the routine word holds the others

parts.note: common means ordinary or routine
end means finish
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Guidance on daily habits that ends up at one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' sets the finish, 'at' and the one inside the routine word, all after the 'about' piece; 'routine' is an adjective here, meaning ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A recommendation is a piece of guidance or counsel.

clue.text: Fruit is gathered in the fall?

indicators.note: gathered in means taken inside, so the word is goes inside the other

parts.note: rainfall, the fall from the sky, is rain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit harvested in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fall' suggests autumn (American usage), but it means water falling from the sky; 'gathered in' sets the little word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a fruit.

clue.text: Evade issue

definitions.meaning: to get away from or avoid
a leak or outflow, as of gas

explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to evade; an escape of gas is an outflow or issue.

clue.text: Is torch I adapted OK for signal?

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Whether a modified flashlight will do for sending a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges IS, TORCH and I. 'signal' is the adjective meaning notable, as in a signal victory, not a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal event is remarkable, one that history will remember.

clue.text: Reduce sail, seeing hazard at sea

definitions.meaning: to take in part of a sail to cut its area
a ridge of rock or coral near the surface

explanation.definitionFit: To reef is to shorten sail; a reef is a rocky ridge that endangers ships.

clue.text: Habitual character in back-street hostelry

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: The usual atmosphere of a pub down a side road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'street hostelry'; 'back' suggests a reversal but the letters run forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit of a person or community.

clue.text: Nelson's area of the ship?

definitions.meaning: a nelson is a wrestling ...; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a wrestling grip, and a ship's cargo space below deck has the same name.

clue.text: Run through short play cut by head of rep

indicators.note: cut by means split open by, so the head letter goes inside

parts.note: a piece is a short dramatic work

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brief play pruned by the repertory company's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes R from 'rep'; 'cut by' puts it inside PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to stab or run through with something sharp.

clue.text: Endearment on a short letter that's flowery

parts.note: pet is an affectionate name, as in 'thanks, pet'
a line is a brief note, as in 'drop me a line'

explanation.surface: A loving pet name added to a florid little note.
explanation.definitionFit: Petaline means like or relating to petals.
